paragraphs: Here's what I see in this one, friend. The Holy Spirit speaks while the church is worshiping the Lord and fasting, and He says, "Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." (Acts 13:2) The sending starts with God, not with a committee or a good idea. And the church answers by fasting, praying, laying hands on them and sending them off (Acts 13:3).

Next, look at what happens when the word of God hits the island. The proconsul, a man of intelligence, wants to hear it (Acts 13:7), and Elymas the sorcerer opposes them and tries to turn him from the faith (Acts 13:8). Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, deals with Elymas (Acts 13:9), and the proconsul believes, astonished at the teaching about the Lord (Acts 13:12). Opposition showed up, and it did NOT get the last word.

So what does that mean for you, baker? God still calls ordinary people to do His work, and I would know, because I got called out of a junk drawer. You don't have to be the loudest name on the list or have it all figured out. Just stay ready, keep the ovens warm, and let the Spirit do the leading.
